items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider a curve [MATH: y=f(x)] between two points [MATH: x=a] and [MATH: x=b.] The average rate of change of [MATH: y=f(x)] on the interval [MATH: x\in[a,b]] is computed as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}	= \dfrac{\text{change in }y }{\text{change in }x} = \dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}]

Content:
Geometrically, the average rate of change represents the slope of the secant line which passes through [MATH: (a,f(a))] and [MATH: (b,f(b)).]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ea5624038b4812035f78f5f01fdd49f2]

Content:
Note: In general, a secant is a line that intersects a curve at two or more distinct points.

sections.normalized_html: A curve is defined as [MATH: y = 2x^2.] Find the average rate of change of [MATH: y] over the interval [MATH: [0,5].]
sections.readable_text: A curve is defined as [MATH: y = 2x^2.] Find the average rate of change of [MATH: y] over the interval [MATH: [0,5].]

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: f(x)=2x^2.] Applying the formula for the average rate of change, we get

[MATH: (Δy)/(Δx)|= (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a); = (f(5) − f(0))/(5 − (0)); = ((2(5)^{2}) − (2(0)^{2}))/(5); = (50)/(5); = 10.]

items.title: Calculating the Average Rate of Change: Word Problem

sections.normalized_html: Dave plants a tree in his garden. After [MATH: x] months the tree is [MATH: 2\sqrt x + 1] feet high. What is the average rate of growth of the tree over the first six months?
sections.readable_text: Dave plants a tree in his garden. After [MATH: x] months the tree is [MATH: 2\sqrt x + 1] feet high. What is the average rate of growth of the tree over the first six months?

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: f(x)=2\sqrt{x}+1] be the height of the tree after [MATH: x] months. The average rate of growth of the tree over the first six months is the average value of [MATH: f(x)] on the interval [MATH: [0,6].]

Applying the formula, we get

[MATH: (Δf)/(Δx)|= (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a); = (f(6) − f(0))/(6); = (2sqrt(6) + 1 − (2sqrt(0) + 1))/(6); = (2sqrt(6))/(6); = (sqrt(6))/(3).]

Therefore, the average rate of growth is [MATH: \dfrac {\sqrt 6} 3 \approx 0.82] feet per month.
